L3.8.1.Source: Data based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled)  through the SebStat system.
L3.8.1.Coverage: Loans Secured by Real Estate granted to all resident sectors and nonresidents: legal entities (excluding counterpart banks) and households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs).
L3.8.1.Dissemination: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
L3.8.1.Units: Million GEL for loan volumes, percent for interest rates.
L3.8.1.Calculations:
Weighted Average Annual Interest Rates on loans (WAIR) are calculated based on the annual interest rates and principal amounts of each loan, following the formula:  (Σ (Principal Amount × Annual Interest Rate)) ÷ (Total principal Amount). Loans with zero interest rates are excluded from calculations.
This methodology is applied to both:
Loan stocks (principal amounts loans at the end of the month) — using principal amounts as weights.
Loan flows (loans granted during the month) — using the principal amounts of loans as weights.
L3.8.1.Definitions:
Loan Secured by Real Estate – a loan collateralized by real estate (land, buildings, constructions).

Annual Interest Rate on loan represents the contractual rate at which interest accrues over one year, expressed as a percentage of the loan amount.

Loan volumes by the end of the Month represent the outstanding principal amount of loans to customers at the end of the reporting period.

Loan volumes during the month represent principal amount of loan inflows granted to customers during a reporting month.

Foreign currency loans are converted into Georgian Lari (GEL) using the official exchange rates as of the end of the reporting month.

L3.12.Source: Data based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled)  through the SebStat system.
L3.12.Coverage: Loans granted by resident banks to all resident sectors: legal entities (including counterpart banks, government and excluding non-bank financial institutions) and households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs).
L3.12.Dissemination: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
L3.12.Definitions:
Loans granted by resident banks are financial assets arising when resident banks provide funds to borrowers under contractual agreements requiring repayment of principal and interest over a specified period.

Loan values represent the outstanding principal amounts of loans (stocks) at the end of the reporting period.

Foreign currency loans are converted into Georgian Lari (GEL) using the official exchange rates as of the end of the reporting month.

Non-financial Sector comprises all resident public and private non-financial corporations as institutional units whose primary activity is the production of goods and non-financial services.

Central Government comprises all resident institutional units that fulfill the functions of government as their primary activity at the central level, exercising authority over the entire economic territory. This includes ministries, departments, agencies, state sub-agencies, Legal Entities of Public Law (LEPLs) operating under central government control, and non-entrepreneurial (non-commercial) legal entities that are controlled and predominantly financed by central government.

Local Government comprises resident government units that exercise authority over only a subdivision of the economic territory, below the level of central government. This includes local self-governing bodies (municipalities), Legal Entities of Public Law (LEPLs) established under and controlled by local government authorities, and non-entrepreneurial (non-commercial) legal entities that are controlled and predominantly financed by local government.

Non-profit Institutions Serving Households (NPISHs) comprises resident non-market non-profit institutions that are not controlled by government and provide goods and services to households free of charge or at prices that are not economically significant.

Banks comprise all resident commercial banks licensed by the National Bank of Georgia (NBG), including those operating on a digital banking model. Licensed microbanks are also included in this sector.

L3.6.Definitions:

LPR.Source: Data based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled)  through the SebStat system.
LPR.Coverage: Loans granted by resident banks to all sectors and nonresidents: legal entities (excluding counterpart banks) and households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs).
LPR.Dissemination: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
LPR.Definitions:
Loans granted by resident banks are financial assets arising when resident banks provide funds to borrowers under contractual agreements requiring repayment of principal and interest over a specified period. Loans are classified based on the original maturity agreed at the time the contract is initiated.

Loan values represent the outstanding principal amounts of loans (stocks) at the end of the reporting period.

Foreign currency loans are converted into Georgian Lari (GEL) using the official exchange rates as of the end of the reporting month.

Mortgage loans are loans for the purchase, construction, or renovation of property.

Auto loans are loans granted for the purchase of motor vehicles, including auto installments, typically secured by the vehicle being financed.

Lombard loans are loans granted against the pledge of easily realizable movable property.

Consumer loans are loans granted to households for various needs.

Business loans for large enterprises are loans granted to finance commercial and business activities of large enterprises, typically based on criteria such as number of employees, turnover, or total assets.

Business loans for SMEs are loans granted to finance commercial and business activities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs),  typically based on criteria such as number of employees, turnover, or total assets.

Other loans are loans that do not fall into the specified purpose categories, including credit cards, overdrafts, installments and loans with unidentified purposes.

LMR.Source: Data based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled)  through the SebStat system.
LMR.Coverage: Loans granted to resident and nonresident households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs).
LMR.Dissemination: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
LMR.Calculations: Interest rates on loan flows are calculated as a weighted average annual interest rate (WAIR) based on the annual interest rates and principal amounts (inflows) of each loan, granted during a month, following the formula:  (Σ (principal inflow amount × annual interest rate)) ÷ (total principal inflow amount). Loans with zero interest rates are excluded from calculations.
LMR.Definitions:
Loans granted by resident banks are financial assets arising when resident banks provide funds to borrowers under contractual agreements requiring repayment of principal and interest over a specified period. Loans are classified based on the original maturity agreed at the time the contract is initiated.

Maturity is an original maturity of all types of loans agreed upon at the time the contract is signed.

Foreign currency loans are converted into Georgian Lari (GEL) using the official exchange rates as of the end of the reporting month.

Interest rate on loans is the annual interest rate on loan inflows during a month. Annual interest rate represents the contractual rate at which interest accrues over one year, expressed as a percentage of the loan amount.

Mortgage loans are loans for the purchase, construction, or renovation of property.

Auto loans are loans granted for the purchase of motor vehicles, including auto installments, typically secured by the vehicle being financed.

Lombard loans are loans granted against the pledge of easily realizable movable property.

Consumer loans are loans granted to households for various needs.

Secured loans are loans backed by collateral, where the lender has a legal claim on specified assets of the borrower in case of default.

Unsecured loans are loans granted without collateral, relying primarily on the borrower’s creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

D3.23.Source: Deposit volumes and interest rates are compiled based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled) through the SebStat system.
D3.23.Coverage: All types of deposits placed by resident and nonresident households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs).
D3.23.Dissemintaion: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
D3.23.Units: Million GEL for deposit volumes, percent for interest rates.
D3.23.Calculations: Weighted Average Annual Interest Rates on deposits (WAIR) are calculated based on the annual interest rates and principal amounts (stocks) of each deposit, following the formula:  (Σ (Principal Amount × Annual Interest Rate)) ÷ (Total principal Amount). Deposits with zero interest rates are excluded from calculations.
D3.23.Definitions:
Deposit volumes show month-end principal amounts (stocks) of all types of deposits placed by all resident and nonresident individuals and individual entrepreneurs.

Annual Interest Rate on deposit represents the contractual rate at which interest accrues over one year, expressed as a percentage of the deposit amount.

Current accounts are funds placed at banks without time restriction to carry out various banking operations.

Demand deposits are funds placed at banks by customers for an indefinite period of time. Demand deposits can be withdrawn on demand and there are no restrictions on depositing or withdrawing these funds. 

Term deposits are funds placed at banks by customers for a predetermined period shown in the corresponding contract. Certificates of Deposit are also included in this category. Term deposits are classified based on the original maturity agreed upon at the time the contract is signed.

Foreign currency deposits are converted into Georgian Lari (GEL) using the official exchange rates as of the end of the reporting month.

D3.22.Source: Interest rates are compiled based on monthly financial data reporting by all resident banks (both domestically and foreign-controlled) through the SebStat system.
D3.22.Coverage: Term deposits placed by all sectors and nonresidents: legal entities (including government) and households (individuals and individual entrepreneurs). Interbank deposits are excluded.
D3.22.Dissemination: Figures are published on the 25th calendar day following the end of the reporting period. If the 25th is a non-working day, publication takes place on the next working day.
D3.22.Calculations: Interest rates on term deposit inflows are calculated as WAIR based on the annual interest rates and principal amounts (inflows) of each deposit, allocated during a month, following the formula:  (Σ (principal inflow amount × annual interest rate)) ÷ (total principal inflow amount). Term deposits with zero interest rates are excluded from calculations.
D3.22.Definitions:
Term deposits are funds placed by customers at resident banks for a predetermined period shown in the corresponding contract. Certificates of Deposit are also included in this category. 

Interest rate on term deposits (i.e. Market Interest Rate) is the annual interest rate on term deposit inflows during a month. Annual interest rate represents the contractual rate at which interest accrues over one year, expressed as a percentage of the deposit amount.
